subtype: Comfort touch in grief and care [Interpreting]
passage: I did not know what to do when Hrithik's father died. We were in the courtyard after the ceremony and Hrithik stood alone, arms crossed, looking at the ground. I wanted to hug him but stopped myself. I am Tejas, and I have known him since school, but I also remember that my own cousin hated being held when she was grieving. So I stood close and said, "Can I hug you, or would you rather I just stay here?" Hrithik was quiet, then nodded and stepped forward. We stood for a while. Afterwards he said asking helped, because he could not have said it himself. I still do not know what was right for anyone else.

qa.q: Where was Hrithik standing after the ceremony?
qa.a: He stood alone in the courtyard.

qa.q: Why did Tejas hold back from hugging at once, and what was Tejas feeling?
qa.a: Tejas wanted to comfort Hrithik but remembered a cousin who hated being held while grieving. Tejas was unsure what suited the friend, so asked first.

qa.q: What made Tejas's approach caring?
qa.a: Tejas asked "Can I hug you" and offered to just stay, so Hrithik could choose either.

qa.q: How might Hrithik have felt when asked, given the crossed arms and silence?
qa.a: Hrithik may have felt too overwhelmed to say what was needed, so a simple question that gave choice was a relief.

grounding: Reflective account of a young adult offering a hug to a grieving friend by asking first and watching for acceptance.

subtype: Comfort touch in grief and care [Interpreting]
passage: Counsellor's note, Thursday. I am Madhuri, the counsellor at the community centre. Vandana lost her brother last month. During the group session, one member reached to hold her shoulder as she began to cry. Vandana went rigid and leaned away, hands in her lap. The member, Sunil, withdrew his hand at once and said, "Sorry. Would you like water instead?" Vandana nodded and drank. A few minutes later she said, "A hug from a friend of mine would be fine, but not from someone I hardly know." I noted that Sunil's quick retreat helped. I will remind the group that asking first respects each person's choice, and I will check on Vandana next week.

qa.q: What did Vandana say she would accept?
qa.a: She said a hug from a friend of hers would be fine, but not from someone she hardly knows.

qa.q: How can you tell Vandana did not want the shoulder touch, and what else might her stiffness mean?
qa.a: She went rigid and leaned away, and later said she prefers hugs from close friends. The stiffness may also have been surprise, but Sunil took no risk and withdrew.

qa.q: What did Sunil do that helped?
qa.a: He took his hand away at once, apologised and offered water instead.

qa.q: What might it be like for Sunil to have his kindness declined?
qa.a: Sunil may have felt embarrassed or unsure, but the quick offer of water shows he cared more about Vandana's comfort than about his gesture.

grounding: Counsellor's note about comfort touch offered to a grieving person, where withdrawal and asking first respect choice.

subtype: Comfort touch in grief and care [Interpreting]
passage:
Sunday night
Went to Afreen's house today, three days after her Ammi passed. The front room was full of aunties and the smell of agarbatti. Afreen was sitting on the floor mat, arms wrapped round her knees, not crying, just very still.
Every part of me wanted to throw my arms round her. But her shoulders were up by her ears, and people kept patting her and she kept flinching a little. So I sat down next to her, not touching, and said quietly, "Can I hug you, or would you rather I just sit?"
She said, "Just sit. For now."
So I sat. We didn't talk. After maybe half an hour she leaned sideways until her head was on my shoulder. I stayed still. I didn't want to break it.
Glad I asked first. Going back tomorrow with food.
Kashish

qa.q: How many days after her Ammi passed did Kashish visit Afreen?
qa.a: Three days after her Ammi passed.

qa.q: What did Kashish notice that made asking before hugging feel right?
qa.a: Kashish felt a strong urge to hug but was concerned and careful, noticing Afreen's raised shoulders and small flinches when people patted her.

qa.q: Why was 'Can I hug you, or would you rather I just sit?' a good question?
qa.a: It gave Afreen a real choice at a time when many people were touching her, so she could accept closeness when she was ready.

qa.q: How might Afreen have felt when she leaned her head on Kashish's shoulder?
qa.a: Afreen may have felt safe and comforted 🤍 enough to seek closeness herself, after being given space rather than more touch.

grounding: Shows a young adult watching a grieving friend's cues and asking before hugging, respecting her choice.

subtype: Comfort touch in grief and care [Interpreting]
passage:
Vijay: heard about your Dadi from Rohit. I'm so sorry
Chaitanya: thanks. still doesn't feel real
Vijay: can I come over after work? I can bring food, or just sit
Chaitanya: yeah. come
(that night)
Vijay: home now. thank you for letting me be there
Vijay: I wasn't sure about hugging you when I walked in. you looked like you might break
Chaitanya: I noticed you stopped at the door
Vijay: I didn't want to grab you if you didn't want it. that's why I asked
Chaitanya: honestly the asking helped. everyone's been hugging me all week without asking and some of it felt like too much
Chaitanya: but yours was the one I actually wanted
Vijay: I'm glad. call any time, even at 3am
Chaitanya: I might

qa.q: Who told Vijay about Chaitanya's Dadi?
qa.a: Rohit.

qa.q: What was Vijay feeling at the door?
qa.a: Vijay felt unsure and protective, worried that Chaitanya 'might break' and that a hug without asking might be unwelcome.

qa.q: Why did asking before hugging help Chaitanya?
qa.a: After a week of unasked-for hugs that sometimes felt like too much, being asked let Chaitanya choose the comfort that was actually wanted.

qa.q: How had the week of hugs felt for Chaitanya?
qa.a: Chaitanya felt overwhelmed by people hugging without asking; some of it felt like too much, even though it was meant kindly.

grounding: Shows a young adult hesitating to hug a grieving friend and asking first, which respects choice and shows care.

subtype: Comfort touch in grief and care [Interpreting]
passage: In the small courtyard in Hoshangabad, the men sat on white sheets and the women had gathered inside. Vaibhav, who taught maths in the classroom next to Yamini's at the government school, sat a little apart, staring at the neem tree. His father had died on Tuesday. Yamini had brought a steel tiffin of khichdi from the staff. She wanted to do more than hand it over; his face looked so empty. But a hug wasn't done here between colleagues, and she wasn't sure even a hand would be welcome. She crouched beside him, set the tiffin down and said quietly, "Vaibhav-ji, can I put a hand on your shoulder? Only if you want." He swallowed and nodded once. She rested her palm lightly on his shoulder. His breath shuddered out, and he bent his head. After a minute she took her hand back and sat with him in silence.

qa.q: What did Yamini bring from the staff?
qa.a: A steel tiffin of khichdi.

qa.q: Why was Yamini unsure about touching Vaibhav?
qa.a: Yamini felt concerned and hesitant, since a hug wasn't done between colleagues there and even a hand might not be welcome to someone grieving.

qa.q: How did Yamini offer comfort respectfully?
qa.a: She crouched beside him, asked quietly whether she could put a hand on his shoulder, waited for his nod, and kept the touch light and brief.

qa.q: What might Vaibhav have felt when her hand rested on his shoulder?
qa.a: Vaibhav may have felt his grief loosen a little, his breath shuddering out, comforted that someone noticed him sitting apart.

grounding: Shows a young adult offering a hand on the shoulder to a grieving colleague only after asking and watching for acceptance.

subtype: Comfort touch in grief and care [Interpreting]
passage:
Felix opened the door of his flat in Leeds in the same grey hoodie he'd worn for three days. His grandmother's funeral had been on Saturday.
Chidi had brought jollof rice in a tub and a speech he'd practised on the bus, but all of it went out of his head. Felix's shoulders were hunched, his arms folded tight across his chest.
Chidi lifted a hand towards his friend's shoulder, then stopped halfway. "Can I hug you? Or not. Either is fine."
Felix stared at the floor. "Not yet. Just... sit with me?"
So they sat on the sofa with the television muted. After a long while, Felix leaned sideways until his shoulder rested against Chidi's. Chidi stayed still, letting him set the pace. When Felix finally cried, Chidi put an arm around him, and Felix didn't pull away.

qa.q: What did Chidi bring to Felix's flat?
qa.a: Chidi brought jollof rice in a tub.

qa.q: What did Felix's folded arms and hunched shoulders suggest?
qa.a: They suggested Felix felt closed in with grief and not ready to be touched; they could also show plain exhaustion after days of mourning.

qa.q: Which choice by Chidi helped most, and why?
qa.a: Asking "Can I hug you?" and accepting "not yet", then sitting quietly, because it let Felix set the pace and come closer when ready.

qa.q: What would change if Chidi had hugged Felix without asking?
qa.a: Felix might have stiffened or felt crowded when he wasn't ready, and he might not have leaned in on his own later.

grounding: A young adult offers comfort to a grieving friend by asking before a hug and watching for signs that touch is welcome.
